content: 1. Dexamethasone has been studied in the context of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2016. The study explored its potential therapeutic effects and outcomes. 2. A review and meta-analysis by Girois et al. in 2006 examined the adverse effects of antifungal therapies in invasive fungal infections, highlighting the risks associated with these treatments. 3. Bicanic et al. (2015) investigated the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate-based induction therapy in patients with HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis, emphasizing the need for careful management of side effects. 4. Bahr et al. (2014) demonstrated that standardized electrolyte supplementation and fluid management significantly improve survival during amphotericin therapy for cryptococcal meningitis in resource-limited settings. 5. Echevarria et al. (2006) evaluated the use of oral rehydration solutions to prevent nephrotoxicity associated with amphotericin B, providing a practical approach to mitigate renal damage. 6. Girmenia et al. (2005) conducted a prospective study on the effects of hydration with salt replacement on renal toxicity during conventional amphotericin B therapy in patients with hematological malignancies. 7. Thakur et al. (2010) showed that supplementing amphotericin B with physiological saline and potassium chloride improved treatment outcomes for kala-azar, a parasitic disease. 8. Park et al. (1999) discussed the use of shunting to treat hydrocephalus secondary to cryptococcal meningitis, providing a surgical option for managing complications. 9. Sun et al. 10. Yuchong et al. (2011) explored the use of lumbar puncture drainage combined with intrathecal amphotericin B injections for controlling cryptococcal meningitis, offering an alternative therapeutic strategy. 11. Meda et al. (2014) conducted an operational research study in Tanzania, demonstrating the effectiveness of serial lumbar punctures using intravenous tubing sets for managing cryptococcal meningitis. 12. Shoham et al. (2005) assessed healthcare providers' adherence to published guidelines for managing cryptococcal disease, identifying gaps in clinical practice. 13. Newton et al. 14. Orem et al. 15. Rex et al. (1993) reported on catastrophic visual loss due to Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis, highlighting the severe complications of delayed or inadequate treatment. 16. Antinori et al. (2005) emphasized the role of cryptococcal antigen assays in diagnosing and monitoring cryptococcal meningitis, underscoring their diagnostic value. 17. Lu et al. (2005) revisited the significance of cryptococcal antigen testing for therapy monitoring in a tertiary Chinese hospital, reinforcing its utility in clinical practice. 18. Dismukes et al. (1987) compared four-week versus six-week combination therapy with amphotericin B and flucytosine for cryptococcal meningitis, providing insights into optimal treatment duration. 19. Powderly et al. (1994) highlighted the importance of measuring cryptococcal antigen in serum and cerebrospinal fluid for managing AIDS-associated cryptococcal meningitis. 20. Haddow et al. (2010) proposed clinical case definitions for cryptococcal immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) in HIV-1-infected individuals, aiding in its recognition and management. 21. Shelburne et al. (2005) discussed the role of IRIS in AIDS-related Cryptococcus neoformans disease during the era of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART). 22. Eshun-Wilson et al. (2018) reviewed the timing of antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation in HIV-positive individuals with cryptococcal meningitis, weighing the benefits of early versus delayed treatment. 23. Bisson et al. (2013) examined the impact of early versus delayed ART initiation on cerebrospinal fluid fungal clearance in adults with HIV and cryptococcal meningitis. 24. Boulware et al. (2014) investigated the timing of ART initiation after diagnosing cryptococcal meningitis, providing evidence for balancing immune recovery and infection control. 25. Makadzange et al. (2010) studied early versus delayed ART initiation in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on concurrent HIV infection and cryptococcal meningitis. 26. Zolopa et al. (2009) demonstrated that early ART reduces AIDS progression and mortality in individuals with acute opportunistic infections. 27. Bicanic et al. (2007) explored fungal burden, early fungicidal activity, and outcomes in cryptococcal meningitis among antiretroviral-naïve and experienced patients treated with amphotericin B or fluconazole. 28. The Southern African HIV Clinicians Society (2013) updated guidelines for preventing, diagnosing, and managing cryptococcal meningitis in HIV-infected individuals. 29. Aberg et al. (2002) conducted a pilot study on discontinuing antifungal therapy for disseminated cryptococcal disease in AIDS patients responding to ART. 30. Kirk et al. (2002) evaluated the safe interruption of maintenance therapy against common HIV-associated opportunistic pathogens during potent ART. 31. Martínez et al. (2000) studied the discontinuation of secondary prophylaxis for cryptococcal meningitis in HIV-infected patients responding to HAART. 32. Mussini et al. (2004) conducted an international observational study on discontinuing maintenance therapy for cryptococcal meningitis in AIDS patients treated with HAART. 33. Rollot et al. (2001) assessed the discontinuation of secondary prophylaxis against cryptococcosis in AIDS patients receiving HAART. 34. Sheng et al. (2002) reported successful discontinuation of fluconazole as secondary prophylaxis for cryptococcosis in AIDS patients responding to HAART. 35. Vibhagool et al. (2003) conducted a prospective, multicenter, randomized study on discontinuing secondary prophylaxis for cryptococcal meningitis in HIV-infected patients treated with HAART. 36. WHO guidelines for diagnosing, preventing, and managing cryptococcal disease in HIV-infected adults, adolescents, and children were updated in 2017, incorporating evidence-based recommendations and addressing resource-limited settings. 37. The guidelines emphasize the use of cryptococcal antigen screening, antifungal therapy, and ART timing to optimize outcomes in cryptococcal meningitis management.
